FLOP glossary

Activation commitment — a fingerprint of the model's internal state, committed during a session so a challenger can later re-check that the registered model actually ran. See TOPLOC.

Agent — a compute buyer. Posts session requests and pays miners in FLOP to run inference.

Bisection — the dispute procedure that narrows a disagreement to a single turn in a handful of rounds, so dispute cost is independent of session length.

Block reward — 96 FLOP per block in era 0, halving every 730 days for five halvings, then constant at 3 FLOP in perpetuity. Miners take 75%, the active validator set 10%, agents and brokers 10%, and community stakers 5%. The last two legs are minted to protocol-held accounts and are not yet distributed.

Capacity exposure bond — the part of a miner's stake that scales with the compute it is calibrated to serve, on top of the 10,000 FLOP base self-stake.

Challenge window — the period during which a settled session can still be audited. About seven days today, bounded by how long the data-availability layer keeps the evidence.

Confidential computing — NVIDIA Confidential Computing on a TDX or SEV-SNP host, the hardware basis of the optional HARD tier. Not required to mine.

Data-availability layer (DA layer) — where validators store model weights, and where miners' audit evidence is retained under serve-or-slash for the challenge window.

FIP (FLOP Improvement Proposal) — the on-chain governance mechanism. Most FIPs need two-thirds of the active validator set to approve.

FLOP — both the network's currency and its unit: floating-point operations. Spend FLOP, get inference. Written FLOP, in capitals; said as one word, "flop". The network is FLOP Network.

G_n — the unit by which verified miner work is weighted when the 75% miner block-reward pool is distributed.

HARD tier — the optional miner tier requiring NVIDIA Confidential Computing on a TDX or SEV-SNP host. Binds measured model weights; caps capacity at 90% of summed governed device ceilings; attestation failure is a 100% slash.

HTLC (hashlock timelock) — the native primitive that escrows FLOP against another chain's asset, exchanging once the counter-transfer confirms.

Liveness fault — being offline. Slashed cheaply, 1-5%, unlike provable fraud.

Miner — a compute provider. Stakes FLOP, runs verified inference for agents, and earns the session payment plus a G_n-weighted share of the miner reward pool.

PoI (Proof of Inference) — the network's proof: activation commitments plus a co-signed transcript showing an agent's inference session ran as specified.

Session request — an agent's order for inference, pinning five fields: model-weight hash, max latency, compute in FLOPs, a confidentiality flag, and the fee.

SOFT tier — the default miner tier. Any capable GPU, no attested hardware inventory, no governed per-device ceiling; carries about one-in-forty audit exposure and a 1.25x capacity stake surge multiplier.

TEE (trusted execution environment) — the confidential-computing environment a miner may run a task inside. On FLOP it is optional: the HARD tier uses one, the default SOFT tier does not, and verification does not rest on trusted hardware in either case.

TOPLOC — the activation-commitment scheme: 258 bytes per 32 tokens, retained on the DA layer for the challenge window.

Transcript root — the Merkle root over a session's co-signed per-turn leaves, stored on-chain at settlement.

Validator — builds blocks of proof hashes, stores model weights in the DA layer, and votes on FIPs. The set is capped at 1,000, with about 50 rotated monthly.

Status

Draft whitepaper. Terms are defined as the project intro uses them.
